migration_report.report_title: Microsoft SQL Server to PostgreSQL Migration Report

equivalency_validation_summary.validation_approach: Tool output only - no agent judgment
equivalency_validation_summary.tool_limitation: SQL Equivalency tool returned UNKNOWN for all complex queries with CTEs, window functions, and multi-statement transactions

changes: Replaced 7 SQL Server statements with PostgreSQL equivalents
Replaced all SQL Server ADO.NET types with Npgsql equivalents
Updated MapProductFromReader to use lowercase column names
Split transaction blocks into separate statements
Removed SQL Server specific parameters (Trusted_Connection, MultipleActiveResultSets, TrustServerCertificate)
Added PostgreSQL parameters (Host, Port, Username, Password)

artifacts_generated: extracted_statements.sql - Catalog of original SQL Server statements

warning_types: Nullable reference warnings (CS8601, CS8618, CS8603, CS8600, CS8625)

remaining_manual_steps: Run schema migration scripts to create tables (products, producthistory, productstats)
Update connection string credentials with actual PostgreSQL username/password
Test all SQL statements with actual PostgreSQL database
Verify transaction behavior matches SQL Server
Run integration tests to validate data integrity

critical_findings.sql_equivalency_tool_limitation: The SQL Equivalency tool was unable to prove equivalency for any of the 7 statement pairs due to complexity of CTEs, window functions, and multi-statement transactions. Manual testing with actual databases is required.
critical_findings.transaction_handling_change: Transaction blocks (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) are now managed at ADO.NET level using NpgsqlTransaction instead of within SQL statements.
critical_findings.schema_naming: DMS tool converted schema: Products → productmanagement_dbo.products. All code respects this naming.
